title: Chapter 142 — Haul-Away Disputes
intro: The crew was supposed to take the old fridge. They refused because it was in the basement.

sections.title: Setting Expectations at Point of Sale
sections.content:
Haul-away disputes almost always start with unclear expectations at the time of sale. The quote should explicitly state: 'Haul-away of [specific old appliance] from [specific location] included.' If the old unit is in a basement, on a second floor, or in a tight space, note that on the delivery ticket so the crew comes prepared.

If haul-away was not quoted, do not assume the customer knows. 'Haul-away of the old unit is $[X] — the team will disconnect it and take it with them. Want me to add that?'

sections.title: When the Crew Refuses
sections.content:
The crew arrives and says the old fridge in the basement is too heavy or the path is too tight. The customer calls you furious.

'I apologize — that should have been flagged when we set up the delivery. Let me schedule a second trip with a crew prepared for the basement removal. I will cover the cost of the return trip since this was our coordination issue.'

The cost of a second trip is far less than the cost of losing the customer.

sections.title: Documentation Prevents Disputes
sections.content:
At point of sale: document the old unit location and access path on the delivery ticket. At pre-delivery confirmation: remind the customer to have the old unit emptied and accessible. At delivery: crew confirms haul-away before they start unboxing the new unit.

Three checkpoints. Zero surprises.
